answer: Each identity is assigned one survey pier. It plants a uniquely cut quartz rod there and may paint an umber baseline ring only from the rod's shadow at solar zenith. Peers return at the next zenith and must recover the same ring-to-rod geometry on that pier. Rods and rings cannot be moved or shared, and a newly seated rod has no valid ring until the following zenith, so every alias must supply its own crystal, its own pigment batch, and sit out a full day before it can be attested.
